question: Why did tiered storage split the remote-storage plugin into a segment-data manager and a separate remote log metadata manager, instead of having the broker discover remote segments by listing the remote store?
gold_facts: Listing an object store such as S3 for metadata is costly (LIST request pricing at many partitions)

gold_evidence.quote: (a) Cost: S3 list object requests cost $0.005 per 1000 requests. If you have 100,000 partitions and want to pull the metadata for each partition at the rate of 1/sec.

But one of the problems of relying on the remote storage to maintain metadata is that tiered-storage needs to be strongly consistent, with an impact not only on the metadata(e.g. LIST in S3) but also on the segment data(e.g. GET after a DELETE in S3).
